'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No data}} | title = [[List of governors of New Mexico|Governor]] | before_election = [[Bill Richardson]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Susana Martínez]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsNM}} The '''2010 New Mexico gubernatorial election''' took place on November 2, 2010. [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] [[Governor of New Mexico|Governor]] [[Bill Richardson]] was [[Term limits in the United States|term limited]] and could not seek a third consecutive term. On June 1, 2010, the Republicans nominated [[Susana Martínez]], the district attorney for [[Doña Ana County, New Mexico]], and the Democrats nominated [[Lieutenant Governor of New Mexico|Lieutenant Governor]] [[Diane Denish]]. While it was initially thought that Richardson would resign early to become [[United States Secretary of Commerce|Secretary of Commerce]] in the [[Obama administration]], Richardson withdrew from the position due to allegations of corruption that were later cleared and he remained governor until the conclusion of his term.{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna28493919|title=Richardson withdrawal leaves cabinet gap|work=[[NBC News]]|date=January 6, 2009|access-date=January 4, 2009}} Susana Martínez won the election on November 2, 2010, and became New Mexico's [[Women in government|first elected female governor]], as well as the first [[Latin Americans|Latina]] governor of any state. ==Primary election== ===Democratic party=== The Democratic [[Partisan primary|primary election]] was held on June 1, 2010.{{cite web|url=https://www.npr.org/blogs/politicaljunkie/2010/01/your_2010_election_calendar.html|title=Your 2010 Election Calendar|date=January 25, 2010|access-date=February 14, 2010|publisher=[[National Public Radio]]|first=Ken|last=Rudin|author-link=Ken Rudin}} ====Candidates==== *[[Diane Denish]], [[Lieutenant Governor of New Mexico|lieutenant governor]]{{cite web|url=http://newmexicoindependent.com/41109/denish-running-for-governor-steps-into-budgetary-fray|title=Denish, running for governor, steps into budgetary fray|date=November 5, 2009|access-date=February 14, 2010|work=[[Center for Independent Media|The New Mexico Independent]]|first=Trip|last=Jennings}} =====Declined===== * [[Val Kilmer]], actor, activist{{Cite web |title=Kilmer pursues role of governor |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2009/02/kilmer-pursues-role-of-governor-019312 |access-date=2025-06-12 |website=POLITICO}}{{Cite web |title=Kilmer says "probably not" running for governor - on March 13, 2010. Susana Martinez was victorious, winning the support of 46.65 percent of delegates, while Allen Weh received 26.32%, Janice Arnold-Jones received 13.16%, Doug Turner won 9.43%, and Pete Domenici Jr. won 4.61%. Candidates who receive less than 20% of the convention vote are required to collect twice as many signatures as those who received 20% in order to appear on the primary ballot.
